evidence.note: Reviewed the rewritten manifest test suite: plan-hash/shard-hash freshness, ignored vs blocking results, filename/id mismatch, duplicate results, cross-shard shape, evidence rule boundary at EvidenceNoteMinLength, and the mrvf- neutralisation tests for both renderers. Assertions match the constants they claim to pin; no TODO/FIXME, no unsafe execution, helpers are deterministic.

Read the end-to-end sharded-review script in full: fixture construction, five pr-ready rounds, the re-cut fix round, ignored foreign-plan result, exit-2 flag rejections with runs.jsonl unchanged, byte-reproducibility of packs, and the task-done path. All temp state is under mktemp with an EXIT trap; every mutating git call runs in a subshell or against an absolute path.

The 'eval' token here is assembled via printf into a fixture text file so the script does not carry the lint pattern literally; it is test data asserting that a staged eval still blocks (line 1150), not executed code. Rubric eval-blocker does not apply.

New golden for `metareview fsm --agent-prompt`. Exit-code semantics (3 / 1+GATE_FAILED / 1+ERR_* / 2), terminal states, and the untrusted-data and consent-knob warnings agree with the contract documented in CLAUDE.md.
Two added assertions require both the codex and claude plugin manifests to advertise workflow runs, matching the existing per-review assertion style in the same file.

findings.note: init_repo runs a bare `cd "$repo"` (not in a subshell), so it permanently changes the script's working directory for everything that follows. It is harmless today because every later command uses an absolute path or its own `(cd ... && ...)` subshell, but the invariant is implicit and a future relative-path addition after `init_repo "$TMP/task"` would silently act on the wrong repo.

evidence.note: bare cd inside init_repo leaks the working directory to the caller
